ROSS TRAWINSKI.
AUG–DEC 2025

UMD Over Terrain Vehicle

Programming & Structures Lead · College Park, MD

Overview

The mission was to drive a 4-wheeled OSV autonomously into a marked zone, locate a magnetic puck sitting on top of a pylon, extract it using a hall-effect sensor to confirm alignment, and return it to a drop zone — all without any driver input once the run started.

As programming and structures lead, I wrote the obstacle-course navigation logic in C++ on Arduino, handling ultrasonic and hall-effect sensor input and the decision-making that let the vehicle find the pylon and avoid the course walls on its own.

On the structures side, I helped design the plywood chassis and the servo-driven lift mechanism that raised and lowered onto the pylon, and worked through a backup rack-and-pinion claw design in case the primary lift didn't pan out.

Alongside the build, I directed a subteam through fabrication, coordinating deliverables with the project manager to keep the schedule on track. On competition day, our team was one of only two out of the whole class to complete every task on the course without error.
